correctness.rationale: RESULT.md lines 5–44 and 46–61: the finite relation language and ultrahomogeneity identify the realized positive distance vectors with complete types over the named points; finite many quantifier-free orbits also imply quantifier elimination and all such types are realized. Every admissible positive vector has arbitrarily many copies mutually at distance 1, by the triangle inequalities and finite extension, so these types are nonalgebraic. The pairwise triangle inequalities reduce to a width condition and a lower bound on the sum of the two smallest entries. A minimum m≥a=ceil(s/2) contributes U_m^n−(U_m−1)^n, while m<a must occur once and gives n B_m^(n−1) with other entries freely in [s−m,min(D,s+m)]. The formula gives D at n=1. The upper sum in fact equals h w^n−(h−1)(w−1)^n: the maximum width occurs h times and smaller widths decrease by one to 1. The maximum short base is strictly less than w for even s with a nonempty short range; for odd s=2k+1≥3 it is min(D−k,2k+1) versus w=min(D−k,2k+2), equal precisely at s≤D≤3k+1. This proves both growth regimes and concentration, including the endpoints, with empty short sums for s=1,2 and the exact constant case D=s=1. value.rationale: Equilateral labelled parameter sets are a natural highly symmetric slice of finite metric type counting. A single exact formula with an inclusive parity/diameter threshold shows that a polynomial prefactor in type growth is tied to a change in geometric behavior: almost every extension in one regime has exactly one short coordinate of the specified distance, while almost none in the other do. This resolves more than a small table or a direct realization criterion.
